notes: The breakout's six header pins (ST, Z, Y, X, GND, VDD) are plugged into breadboard row j, columns 4-9. The image shows rows f-j in the top half, which the catalogue calls bank 'b'. I used that naming.
Column numbers and rows were read from the image, so they are approximate. Each jumper wire shares a column strip with its module pin, so the electrical result doesn't depend on the exact row.

Pin mapping follows the manual's table: A0=Self-Test, A1=Z, A2=Y, A3=X, A4=GND (driven LOW in code), A5=VDD (driven HIGH in code). The schematic shows X/Y/Z crossing, but the table and the circuit image agree with the mapping above.
The ADXL335 catalogue part's VCC port stands for the breakout's VDD pin.
Power and ground come from Arduino analog pins A5 and A4 used as digital outputs. The 5V and GND pins aren't used.
